findings.title: Cleanup job interval accidentally reduced from 10 minutes to 1
findings.body: Run() now starts the cleanup ticker at 1 minute instead of 10. Nothing in this change describes or tests a schedule change, and clean() still uses a 9-minute timeout, so this looks like leftover debug. After merge, annotation cleanup (and every other cleanup job) runs about 10x more often, increasing DB load and lock contention—the opposite of the deadlock fix—and a slow run can still be in progress when the next tick is due.

findings.title: Leftover Error logs dump every cleanup batch, including all IDs
findings.body: CleanAnnotations and CleanOrphanedAnnotationTags log successful fetch/delete steps with log.Error, including the full ID slice and SQL condition (lines 534, 537, 554, 557, 576, and 579). These fire on every batch, even when nothing is deleted. In production that spams error-level logs and can serialize tens of thousands of IDs per batch (the new test uses a batch size of 32767), adding load and drowning real errors. These should be removed or dropped to debug without the ID list.
